subject: genetics
question: **Type:** application A researcher compares two double stranded DNA molecules that are the same length. Molecule 1 is 70 percent GC and molecule 2 is 30 percent GC. Why does molecule 1 separate into single strands at a higher temperature?

options.text: A G=C base pair is held together by two hydrogen bonds, fewer than the three bonds of an A=T pair.
The sugar phosphate backbone of a GC rich molecule carries more phosphodiester bonds per unit length.
Guanine and cytosine are larger bases, so the helix of molecule 1 is physically harder to pull apart.
A G=C base pair is held together by three hydrogen bonds, while an A=T pair forms only two.

explanation: A G=C base pair is joined by three hydrogen bonds whereas an A=T pair is joined by two, so a molecule with more GC pairs needs more energy to separate its strands and melts at a higher temperature. Option A has the bond counts reversed, option B is wrong because every base pair sits in the same sugar phosphate backbone, and option C incorrectly invokes base size. Counting hydrogen bonds, not backbone or size differences, predicts the melting behavior.
